# Gauge Cluster LED Color Change

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Remove gauges, swap 1206 SMD Cool Clear White LED's with a fine tipped soldering iron, and reinstall the needles. [t765]

[Partial] Source, cut, and apply transparent colored vinyl sheets to change the gauge cluster LED color. [t765]

- Fine tipped soldering iron [t765]

- Small flat tip screwdrivers [t765]
- Scissors [t765]
- Long razor blade [t765]
- Blow dryer [t765]
- [Partial] Clear head (steady hands) [t765]
- Auto painters tape or similar [t765]

## Parts

- 1206 SMD Cool Clear White LED's: Quantity of 50, sourced from Lighthouse LEDs [t765]
- Transparent colored vinyl: 3 sheets of 8x12 inch adhesive coated vinyl [t765]
- Vinyl transparent sheets: 3 sheets for coloring overlays [t765]

## Tips & gotchas

- Look for solid triangles on the circuit board to indicate current direction if lacking a multimeter. [t765]
- Identify LED negative side by looking down at the top where green tint shows. [t765]
- Use an old towel under the work area to protect against dirt and scratches. [t765]

## Common mistakes

- [Partial] Installing LEDs backward requiring rework [t765]
- [Partial] Overheating new LEDs causing them to fall apart [t765]
